title: Two-point convex bandits in a general norm with Euclidean-Lipschitz losses
summary: Action centers lie in a convex set with public mirror geometry, and losses are globally Euclidean Lipschitz. Each round reveals exact values of the same function on opposite sides of the center; only the center incurs loss. Dual-norm moments of spherical directions control the gradient-estimator variance.

model.instance: The compact convex center-action set $W\subset\mathbb R^d$, norm $\|\cdot\|$, and its dual are public. The regularizer $\psi$ is $1$-strongly convex in that norm and satisfies $$0\le\psi(x)\le R_\psi^2\quad(x\in W),\qquad p_*\ge\left(\mathbb E_{u\sim\operatorname{Unif}(\mathbb S^{d-1})}\|u\|_*^4\right)^{1/4}.$$. All losses are fixed before interaction, convex on all of $\mathbb R^d$, and $G_2$-Lipschitz in the Euclidean norm.

operations.query_signature: $$f_t(x_t+\rho_tu_t),\qquad f_t(x_t-\rho_tu_t).$$ Both evaluations use the same current function without measurement noise, and are revealed after the probes are submitted. The center satisfies $x_t\in W$; probes may lie outside $W$ because losses are defined on the whole space. Loss is incurred only at the center $x_t$. Causal learners keep centers feasible. Inputs $W,\psi,\|\cdot\|,G_2,R_\psi,p_*,T$ are public, and one mirror/proximal update is allowed per round. Received feedback may be stored and reused computationally. No unrevealed historical information or extra queries to exhausted samples are available; any within-round full-function or common-sample access must be explicit.

metric.base_expression: $$R_T=\sum_{t=1}^T f_t(w_t)-\min_{w\in W}\sum_{t=1}^T f_t(w).$$ Only the feasible center incurs loss; losses at the two exact-value probes are not added.

metric.finiteness_conditions: The center domain W is compact and therefore has finite Euclidean diameter. Loss differences between centers are bounded by G_2 times that diameter.

regimes.predicate_text: Choose step size $\eta_{\mathrm{step}}=R_\psi/(p_*G_2\sqrt{dT})$ and probe radius satisfying $0<\rho_t\le p_*R_\psi\sqrt{d/T}$. The quantity $p_*$ bounds the fourth moment of the dual norm of a spherical direction; $G_2$ is the Euclidean Lipschitz constant, and $R_\psi$ comes from the range condition on the regularizer $0\le\psi\le R_\psi^2$. Both probes are submitted together and return exact values of the same function. Only the center incurs loss. Here $\eta_{\mathrm{step}}$ is the update step size, unrelated to exp-concavity.
